title: AI Supply Chain Obligations Under EU AI Act Article 28
context: 2026-08-26 engine cycle -- 14-board measurement fleet running on RunPod A100
body: Article 28 of the EU AI Act formalises the AI value chain: any distributor, importer, or deployer who significantly modifies a high-risk AI system inherits the obligations of a provider. This is not a passive supply chain — it is an active liability cascade. Every intermediary who rebrands, retunes, or repurposes a model becomes accountable for conformity assessment, documentation, and incident reporting. For purchasers and deployers, this means: (1) your procurement checklist must verify whether the upstream supplier claims provider status or not, (2) any fine-tuning, prompt-engineering system layer, or safety-wrapper modification may constitute a substantial modification that re-triggers the entire conformity cycle, (3) the August 2026 Code of Practice on General-Purpose AI adds a transparency layer — all GP-AI model providers must publish a sufficiently detailed summary of training data and downstream-system documentation. A verified measurement credential becomes critical here: without a signed, auditable record of what the model was and who modified it, the entire chain is unverifiable. The Council of AI recommendation: treat every downstream AI integration as a new provider moment until a competent authority has reviewed the modification boundary. Monitored containment — instrumented boundary watching — is the minimum posture for any deployer touching a high-risk supply chain node.
